name: Landsat Connect (AsturExplorers)
tagline: Pin a spot, get told before Landsat flies over, then compare your ground measurement with the 3×3 pixel it captured.
problem: Comparing ground measurements with Landsat surface reflectance means knowing when the satellite passes and then finding the right pixel — tedious for non-specialists.
solution: A designed web app (Figma prototype plus planned Django architecture): users save locations on a map, choose notification lead time and channel (email, SMS, push), get alerts before an overpass and when data is ready, then view a 3×3 pixel grid with metadata and spectral signature, filter by cloud cover and export CSV or PDF. Accessibility is specified (WCAG 2.1, localization, offline cache).

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won the award for the most plausible concept and design.
Provides a simple, intuitive way to track Landsat satellites, access surface reflectance data, set a target location and receive overpass notifications.
Designed for users of all technical levels and abilities, with concrete use cases for farmers, conservation researchers and urban planners.
The concept award rewarded a complete, accessible design that follows the challenge brief closely, even though the deliverable was a prototype rather than running software.

lessons: A thorough design with use cases and accessibility can win the concept award without a deployed build.
Answer every clause of the brief (location, notification, data access) visibly in the design.

sources.note: Team-written features, use cases, planned architecture, accessibility, Figma project link; AI used for research, logo and video voice-over.
